name: Sick of It All
label: Revelation
lede: [[Lou Koller]] and [[Pete Koller]] started the band in their parents' Queens basement, and Revelation is still pressing that first seven-inch in new colors. They carried New York hardcore from the CBGB matinees to MTV to festival fields, and in the band's 40th year Lou died.

eras.title: Scared to death at the Right Track Inn
eras.text: Lou Koller and Pete Koller jammed in their parents' Queens basement during the summer weeks the folks were away. Within a year they'd gone from a nervous opening slot on Long Island to the CBGB matinees and the third record on a brand-new label called Revelation.

years.h: Craig Setari books them as a "special guest"
years.p: Lou Koller on the night of May 17, 1986. The Right Track Inn bill on Long Island also had [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Straight Ahead|1fd60d7c-dc35-44f5-9162-4113b6ca4a69]] and Crippled Youth, and the band had rehearsed for a month.
years.xp:
Setari listed the unknown band as a special guest at first. Lou Koller says they played their own songs early, then closed with a [[Cause for Alarm|1940001f-3270-4d87-9501-eb243d5f9f50]] cover the crowd already knew.

Lou has also described the basement where it started: his parents went away for two weeks each summer, and the band jammed in Queens while the neighbors stood outside, bothered by the volume. Setari would join the band seven years later and stay for the next three decades.

years.h: Rich Cipriano and Armand Majidi take over the rhythm section
years.p: The original drummer and bassist are gone after the first show. [[Rich Cipriano|fe1b3bb1-f4b1-4359-b308-30247a89e9d8]] takes bass, [[Armand Majidi|5835deec-ae60-4ac0-888e-5b5e70270d0f]] takes drums, and that pair makes the early records.

years.h: A demo gets them onto the CBGB Sunday matinees
years.p: After a self-titled demo, the band lands regular spots on the hardcore matinees at CBGB on the Bowery.

years.h: The dragon debuts on Revelation No. 3
years.p: A thousand hand-numbered black copies, with no Rev logo on the A-side art. The dragon, drawn in the spirit of a Greg Irons tattoo flash sheet, comes back on seven of their studio albums.
years.xp: Revelation has kept the record alive ever since: a numbered red second press, 300 black copies for a Gilman Street record convention, a 33 rpm run, a 10th-anniversary repress in 1997, then clear vinyl for Record Store Day 2010 and a string of colors after that.

eras.title: Seven albums on paper, a revolving door in the van
eras.text: A deal with Relativity put the band on the road with Agnostic Front, Bad Brains and Exodus. The records got bigger while the rhythm section kept changing, and one EP carried photos of members who'd already left.

years.h: A Revelation single turns into a seven-album deal at Relativity
years.p: [[Lou Koller|f1549cac-a48c-4741-8edd-09c1016ada64]] and [[Pete Koller|dfa89132-3c8b-41f3-a1ed-cf388d836386]] now open for [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]], [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]] and, for five East Coast dates, the thrash band Exodus.

years.h: Blood, Sweat, and No Tears, the debut LP
years.p: Relativity, 1989. Kerrang! would later say it helped change what the world meant by New York hardcore.
years.xp: Lou was unhappy with how the video for Injustice System turned out.

years.h: Two weeks on the West Coast behind Bad Brains
years.p: After headline runs of their own, the band supports [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] on the Quickness tour with [[Leeway|121193a5-cb8b-4182-968c-8ba607856fa2]].

years.h: Max Capshaw sits in while Majidi plays with Rest in Pieces
years.p: Majidi is back for a national run with [[D.R.I.|95f6e954-8bed-4f8e-a53e-d155bb6f7ace]]. Lou's later verdict on [[Max Capshaw|74d0e618-1149-46b2-898b-7169b7f9819d]] was that he was too young.

years.h: Cipriano and Majidi both leave before an Agnostic Front tour
years.p: [[Eddie Coen|6c1ec806-8c9e-4a6f-be2f-ae0d940e0f30]] and [[Eric Komst|bba140d0-01c1-4a77-a596-30f376822207]] step in for the tour with [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]].
years.xp: Coen soon left for the Cycle Sluts from Hell, and Komst was eventually fired.

years.h: An EP pictures two members who had already left
years.p: The We Stand Alone cover shows Coen and Komst anyway, so fans would see a band still standing. By the next album Majidi and Cipriano are back.
years.xp: That year the band toured with [[Sepultura|1d93c839-22e7-4f76-ad84-d27039efc048]], [[Napalm Death|ce7bba8b-026b-4aa6-bddb-f98ed6d595e4]] and Sacred Reich on the New Titans on the Bloc tour.

years.h: Just Look Around sends them to Europe twice
years.p: The second Relativity LP is followed by a spring run through Europe and a winter tour of the continent.

eras.title: Hardcore on Headbangers Ball
eras.text: With Craig Setari on bass the line-up locked in for good, and East West moved the band to a major. Scratch the Surface got a New York hardcore video into MTV rotation and sent them to Japan, South America and New Zealand.

years.h: Craig Setari, who booked the first show, joins on bass
years.p: He replaces Cipriano in early 1993. With Lou, Pete and Majidi, it's the line-up for the next thirty-plus years.
years.xp: By the end of 1993 came shows in Japan, a live album called Live in a World Full of Hate and a deal with East West.

years.h: Scratch the Surface takes the band around the world
years.p: Their first album to chart, debuting at No. 67 in Germany. The title-track video premieres on MTV's Headbangers Ball, and Step Down goes into rotation.
years.xp:
Vice's Mike Hill called it the album that took NYHC worldwide, making the band the closest thing hardcore had to a household name. Step Down even turned up on Beavis and Butt-Head.

The touring never let up: two weeks with [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]], a November run behind [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]] and [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]], ten shows with [[Black Train Jack|be939900-e334-431e-b85a-c62f4ec3bf60]], then the Americas, Europe, Japan and New Zealand.

years.h: Korn open for them, then comes the first Warped Tour
years.p: A US headline run from January to March, with [[Korn|ac865b2e-bba8-4f5a-8756-dd40d5e39f46]], Orange 9mm and Trial, then a slot on the very first Warped Tour.

years.h: Built to Last, their one album for Elektra
years.p: Elektra is East West's sister label. The record holds set staples Us vs. Them, Busted and Good Lookin' Out.
years.xp: The same year Revelation reissued the 1987 debut seven-inch for its tenth birthday.

eras.title: Off the majors, onto Fat Wreck Chords
eras.text: NOFX frontman Fat Mike's label took them in, and the band went back to the road. Slayer members found them in Argentina, and by the 20th birthday younger bands were lining up to cover them.

years.h: Slayer catch them in Argentina, and Call to Arms follows
years.p: Earlier in 1999, [[Slayer|bdacc37b-8633-4bf8-9dd5-4662ee651aec]] members see the band play in Argentina. Later that year they tour with Slayer and [[Meshuggah|cf8b3b8c-118e-4136-8d1d-c37091173413]].
years.xp: The band signed to Fat Mike's Fat Wreck Chords in 1998. Call to Arms opened with the Potential for a Fall single.

years.h: Lou Koller wonders about the cover of Yours Truly
years.p: Critics were cooler on the 2000 album, though District and Blown Away became fan favorites. Lou later suggested the cover art may have hurt how it was received.

years.h: Death to Tyrants goes to Abacus
years.p: A new label under the Century Media umbrella. Critics heard an album from a band that hadn't slowed down.

years.cap: Craig Setari on bass, Eurockeennes festival, July 2007
years.h: Twenty years in, they play B.B. King's on 42nd Street
years.p: Times Square is a long way from the Right Track Inn on Long Island.

years.h: Our Impact Will Be Felt has everyone covering them
years.p: [[Sepultura|1d93c839-22e7-4f76-ad84-d27039efc048]], [[Napalm Death|ce7bba8b-026b-4aa6-bddb-f98ed6d595e4]], [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]], [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]], Bouncing Souls, [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]], [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]] and more play Sick of It All songs on the tribute album.

eras.title: Thirty years, front to back
eras.text: On Century Media, the band marked anniversaries by getting in the van. They played whole albums start to finish, and in 2020 the brothers put the story in a book.

years.h: They record in Copenhagen instead of New York
years.p: Based on a True Story is the first album for Century Media, made with producer Tue Madsen.

years.cap: Lou Koller points into the crowd, Vainstream Rockfest, July 2015
years.h: Two albums front to back at Fun Fun Fun Fest
years.p: The year of The Last Act of Defiance, the band plays Scratch the Surface and Blood, Sweat, and No Tears all the way through in Austin.

years.cap: Lou Koller at Hellfest, June 2016, the band's thirtieth year
years.h: Thirty years in, a hometown night at Webster Hall
years.p: [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]] are on the bill, mid-way through a world tour for the milestone. When the Smoke Clears, an EP of new songs, follows on November 4.

years.cap: Lou Koller in front of the dragon backdrop, Full Force festival, June 2019
q: We wanted to show the world what we loved.
years.h: The 1987 dragon gets its own album title
years.p: Wake the Sleeping Dragon! comes out November 2. Around then Lou pushed back on calling the band the Kings of New York hardcore.
years.xp: Lou preferred ambassadors to kings. It fit a group that had spent thirty years bringing New York hardcore to Brazil, Japan and German festival fields.

years.cap: Lou Koller leaning off the stage rig, Full Force festival, June 2019
years.h: With touring shut down, the Kollers write the book
years.p: Lou and Pete publish The Blood and Sweat: The Story of Sick of It All's Koller Brothers. Decibel called it one of the best books ever written about hardcore.

eras.title: The last fight
eras.text: Pete sat out a 2022 tour for surgery. Then Lou's esophageal cancer pulled the band off the road, the scene he helped build rallied around him, and in the band's 40th year he died.

years.h: Pete Koller sits out the European tour for hernia surgery
years.p: Craig Silverman fills in on guitar, and Pete is back afterward, as Blabbermouth and Wikipedia report.

years.h: Lou Koller says he has esophageal cancer
years.p: Rolling Stone reported it as a tumor diagnosis. Treatment starts that summer, and the band's July European dates are cancelled.

yt: Lou Koller on video at the benefit
years.h: Life of Agony and Municipal Waste play a benefit for Lou
years.p: [[Life of Agony|d6ff259a-bbb6-4454-8503-80151da5f2db]], [[Municipal Waste|b5a31e9b-1fa2-45f9-91f5-b3a25fb38038]], [[Crown of Thornz|e7b3e015-81fa-4180-aa7b-7bfcf821209d]] and [[Vision of Disorder|618a18b1-dec3-4c4a-813b-988d9c065722]] play the show for the Sick of It All singer.

years.h: Cancer free in May, back in late September
years.p: Lou announced in May 2025 that he was officially cancer free. In late September he tells fans it has returned.
years.xp: In between, in August, Craig Setari said new music was in the works, with shows planned for 2026.

years.src: Blabbermouth · Arrow Lords of Metal · Wikipedia
years.h: By December, the tumors are neither growing nor shrinking
years.p: Lou calls his treatment a stalemate. Pete says his brother lost 70 pounds and was put on a feeding tube, as Blabbermouth reported.

years.h: Lou Koller dies in hospice care in the band's 40th year
years.p: He died in Matawan, New Jersey, after a two-year fight with esophageal cancer, survived by his wife Melissa, his daughter and his brother Pete.
years.xp: The band wrote that it was announcing the news to its worldwide hardcore family, and called him a beloved friend and a frontman.

years.h: Pete Koller says Lou asked the band to keep going
years.p: In an Instagram video, Pete says his brother wanted Sick of It All to continue, and that the band is working out how to honor that.
